title: UP BOARD CLASS 10 — Chemistry | Displacement Double Displacement
description: Subject-wise test on Displacement Double Displacement (Chemistry) for UP BOARD CLASS 10. 25Q.
subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following reactions is a displacement reaction?

options.explanation: This is a neutralization reaction, not a displacement reaction.
This is a decomposition reaction, not a displacement reaction.
Iron (Fe) is more reactive than copper (Cu) and displaces it from copper sulphate solution.
This is a double displacement reaction, not a displacement reaction.

questions.explanation: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Identify the double displacement reaction among the following:

options.explanation: This is a combustion reaction, not a double displacement reaction.
This is an electrolysis reaction, not a double displacement reaction.
Barium chloride reacts with sodium sulphate to form barium sulphate (a precipitate) and sodium chloride by exchanging their respective ions.
This is a displacement reaction, not a double displacement reaction.

questions.explanation: A double displacement reaction involves the exchange of ions between two reactant compounds.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following metals can displace hydrogen from dilute acids?

options.explanation: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen and cannot displace it from dilute acids.
Silver is less reactive than hydrogen and cannot displace it from dilute acids.
Zinc is more reactive than hydrogen and can displace it from dilute acids.
Gold is less reactive than hydrogen and cannot displace it from dilute acids.

questions.explanation: Metals that are more reactive than hydrogen can displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: When lead nitrate solution is mixed with potassium iodide solution, what is the color of the precipitate formed?

options.explanation: The precipitate formed is not white.
The precipitate formed is not blue.
The precipitate formed is bright yellow.
The precipitate formed is not green.

questions.explanation: The reaction between lead nitrate and potassium iodide forms lead iodide, which is a bright yellow precipitate.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: When a strip of zinc metal is placed in a copper sulphate solution, what observation is correct and what type of reaction occurs?

options.explanation: A reaction does occur, and it is not a combination reaction.

options.text: Blue color of solution fades and reddish-brown deposit is formed; Displacement reaction.
options.explanation: The blue color of copper sulphate solution fades due to the formation of colorless zinc sulphate, and reddish-brown copper metal is deposited.

options.text: Solution turns green and gas bubbles are produced; Decomposition reaction.
options.explanation: The solution does not turn green, and gas bubbles are not produced.

options.text: White precipitate is formed; Double displacement reaction.
options.explanation: A reddish-brown deposit is formed, not a white precipitate, and it is a displacement reaction, not a double displacement reaction.

questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces it from copper sulphate solution to form zinc sulphate and copper metal.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a displacement reaction?

options.explanation: This is a combination reaction.
This is a decomposition reaction.
Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.

questions.explanation: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.

questions.question: A chemical reaction in which two different atoms or groups of atoms are exchanged between two compounds to form two new compounds is generally known as a:

options.explanation: In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a new substance.
In a decomposition reaction, a single substance breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
In a double displacement reaction, two different atoms or groups of atoms are exchanged between two compounds to form two new compounds.

questions.explanation: The definition given describes a double displacement reaction, where ions or groups of ions exchange places.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following metals is capable of displacing hydrogen from dilute acids?

options.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
Zinc is above hydrogen in the reactivity series and can displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Silver is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
Gold is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

questions.explanation: Metals higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Most double displacement reactions are characterized by the formation of a:

options.explanation: Some double displacement reactions may produce a gas, but it is not the most common characteristic.
Double displacement reactions do not typically produce a liquid product.
Many double displacement reactions produce a precipitate, which is an insoluble solid product.
While some double displacement reactions may produce a soluble salt, it is not the most common characteristic.

questions.explanation: Many double displacement reactions are precipitation reactions, where two soluble ionic compounds react to form an insoluble solid product called a precipitate.

questions.question: When a strip of zinc metal is dipped in a solution of copper sulphate, what observable change occurs?

options.text: The solution turns green and the zinc strip becomes shiny.
options.explanation: The solution does not turn green, and the zinc strip does not become shiny.

options.text: The solution remains blue and the zinc strip dissolves completely.
options.explanation: The solution does not remain blue, and the zinc strip does not dissolve completely.

options.text: The blue solution turns colourless, and a reddish-brown deposit forms on the zinc strip.
options.explanation: The blue colour of CuSO₄ solution fades (turns colourless due to formation of ZnSO₄, which is colourless), and reddish-brown copper metal is deposited on the zinc strip.

options.text: The blue solution turns green, and a black deposit forms on the zinc strip.
options.explanation: The solution does not turn green, and a black deposit does not form on the zinc strip.

questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper. It displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.

questions.question: When an aqueous solution of barium chloride is mixed with an aqueous solution of sodium sulphate, a white precipitate is formed. The chemical name of this white precipitate is:

options.explanation: Sodium chloride is a soluble salt and is not the precipitate formed in this reaction.
Barium nitrate is not formed in this reaction.
Barium sulphate is the insoluble white solid that forms the precipitate in this reaction.
Sodium sulphate is a soluble salt and is not the precipitate formed in this reaction.

questions.explanation: The reaction is BaCl₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq). Barium sulphate (BaSO₄) is an insoluble white solid, which forms the precipitate.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): When an iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution, a brown coating of copper is formed on the iron nail. Reason (R): Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces copper from its salt solution.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true; iron is more reactive than copper.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true; a brown coating of copper is formed on the iron nail.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true; the brown coating is indeed copper deposited due to displacement. Reason (R) is also true; iron is higher in the reactivity series than copper.

questions.question: When an iron nail is dipped in a copper sulphate solution, the blue colour of the solution gradually fades and a reddish-brown deposit appears on the iron nail. The fading of the blue colour is due to the formation of:

options.explanation: Copper oxide is not formed in this reaction.
Iron(II) sulphate is formed when iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
Copper(II) sulphate is the reactant, not the product, in this reaction.
Iron(III) oxide is not formed in this reaction.

questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate (blue solution) to form iron(II) sulphate (light green solution) and solid copper (reddish-brown deposit).

questions.question: Which of the following reactions will *not* occur?

options.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so this displacement reaction can occur.
Iron is less reactive than zinc, but this reaction can still occur because iron is more reactive than zinc in some cases.
Magnesium is more reactive than iron, so this displacement reaction can occur.
Copper is less reactive than magnesium, so copper cannot displace magnesium from magnesium sulphate solution.

questions.explanation: A displacement reaction occurs only if the displacing element is more reactive than the element it is displacing.

questions.question: In the reaction between lead nitrate solution and potassium iodide solution, a yellow precipitate is formed. The chemical formula of this yellow precipitate is:

Pb(NO₃)₂ is the reactant, not the precipitate.
PbI₂ is the yellow precipitate formed in the reaction.

questions.question: A student performs two experiments. Experiment 1: He adds a metal 'M' to an aqueous solution of iron(II) sulphate, and observes that the green colour of the solution fades and a grey solid settles at the bottom. Experiment 2: He mixes aqueous solutions of 'P' and 'Q' and observes a white precipitate forming. Based on these observations, identify the type of reactions occurring in Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, respectively.

options.explanation: The order of the reactions is incorrect.
Experiment 1 is a Displacement reaction, and Experiment 2 is a Double Displacement reaction.
Experiment 2 is a Double Displacement reaction, not a Displacement reaction.
Experiment 1 is a Displacement reaction, not a Double Displacement reaction.

questions.explanation: Experiment 1 is a Displacement reaction, and Experiment 2 is a Double Displacement reaction.

questions.question: If X is a metal from the reactivity series between magnesium and copper, which of the following could be X in the reaction X + 2HCl → XCl₂ + H₂?

options.explanation: Sodium is too reactive and would displace hydrogen violently, producing a different reaction.
While zinc can displace hydrogen, it is not between magnesium and copper in the reactivity series.
Iron lies between magnesium and copper in the reactivity series and can displace hydrogen from dilute HCl, forming FeCl₂ and H₂ gas.
Silver is less reactive than hydrogen and would not displace it from dilute HCl.

questions.explanation: The metal X must be able to displace hydrogen from dilute HCl, which means it must be more reactive than hydrogen but less reactive than magnesium.
